fields.title: [B17] DB 정리 (긴 영어)
fields.body: This note summarizes how a relational database answers a query. A SELECT statement lists the columns, the FROM clause names the table, and the WHERE clause filters rows. You can ORDER BY a column, GROUP BY a key, and use UNION to merge two result sets that have the same columns. An INSERT adds rows, an UPDATE changes them, and a DELETE removes them. Indexes speed up lookups, while a JOIN combines rows from two tables on a matching key. Always use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation so that user input is never treated as code.
